label: copy phase (after the delimiter step)
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature: fires on about 92% of copy-phase steps (t > L, recall_idx >= 1), and those steps hold 99.8% of the activation mass. It is almost silent during the original-token phase (0.3% of steps, none at t < 3) and on the <DEL> delimiter step itself (1%). Its rate does not depend on input token, output token, L, digit count or first token. Magnitude varies within a sequence: the top examples peak at the early copy steps (recall_idx 1-3) and fall off afterward, sometimes rising again near the end. Output tokens c/d/f/0 carry slightly more mass than y/b/o. The rare misses are weak activations just before or at <DEL>, and the ~8% false positives are copy steps where it is silent.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. On the test split, phase==2 scores P 0.923, R 0.994, F1 0.957, mass recall 0.998. The feature is silent at t<3 and fires on about 1% of delimiter steps and 0.3% of original-phase steps, as claimed.

The claim that the firing rate does not depend on input or output token is false; the profile's per-token tables only list the top tokens. Copy-phase rate by in_tok: p 0.36 and g 0.71, against about 0.93-0.96 for every other token. By out_tok: a/c/d/e/f/0/w/q/u fire on about 99.9-100% of copy steps, while g fires on 0.71, p 0.76, 2 0.79, h 0.80, 1 0.81, l 0.84 and i 0.86. Most of the 8% false positives fall in this token-dependent class, not scattered noise.

The two effects interact. When in_tok is p and out_tok is one of a/c/d/f/0, the feature fires 99.7% of the time. When in_tok is p and out_tok is one of g/p/h/2, it almost never fires. So the silent copy steps are mostly 'input p (or g), output in a weak set'.

The magnitude description is off. Calling the out_tok effect 'slightly more mass' understates it: out_tok c/d each carry 0.075 of the mass versus 0.029 for y, about 2.5x on similar step counts. In the top examples the peak lands on the step whose output is c/d/0/f, often just before a run like 'd d' or 'c c', and not consistently at recall_idx 1-3 (for example it peaks at recall_idx 5-6 in 'b h 2 3 h d d 0 r' and 'k k s f s c c 0 0'). By recall_idx, the mass share falls in step with how many sequences reach that index, so the 'peaks early' claim is not specific.
